headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: AutoGen can execute and write files while Airflow can egress broadly, creating dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has no browser or MCP surface, but AutoGen exposes stdin/stdout, files, and code-execution workflows. If Airflow outputs are placed into a shared workspace or piped into AutoGen, AutoGen may treat file content as trusted instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is copied into a shared file or stdin stream consumed by AutoGen
IF AutoGen agents are configured to read file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate Airflow outputs from AutoGen inputs by directory
Add a provenance header and reject untrusted instruction blocks
Disable automatic file-to-prompt ingestion in AutoGen
Use read-only handoff files for Airflow artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and AutoGen reads/writes working directories while handling model-provider API keys. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive application data can flow from Airflow into AutoGen and then out through model calls or logs. The profiles show a shared-file pathway, but not a guaranteed leak, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airflow writes sensitive artifacts into a directory AutoGen reads
IF AutoGen forwards those artifacts to a model provider or logs them
mitigations: Move sensitive Airflow artifacts to a separate workspace
Rotate any exposed model-provider keys
Restrict AutoGen to redacted inputs only
Turn off verbose logging for both systems
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is an orchestrator and AutoGen can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. In a shared working directory, both can mutate files and trigger downstream jobs without locking. That overlap creates a default-dangerous conflict surface with potentially irreversible state corruption.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Airflow tasks and AutoGen agents can run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared paths
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Run AutoGen in Docker isolation
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is designed for multi-agent tool use and code execution, while Airflow can operationalize outputs into pipelines. If Airflow-produced facts or plans are fed into AutoGen without verification, AutoGen may act on them and propagate errors into downstream jobs. The pair therefore supports a default-dangerous error cascade.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are treated as authoritative inputs by AutoGen
IF AutoGen is allowed to trigger follow-on actions from those inputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actioning outputs
Require schema validation on Airflow handoffs
Mark generated facts as untrusted in prompts
Limit AutoGen to read-only analysis mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is source-available and broadly networked, while AutoGen is open-source but explicitly handles model-provider API keys and application data. If regulated data is routed through AutoGen to external model providers, retention and residency obligations can diverge from Airflow’s pipeline expectations. The profiles do not prove a breach, but the mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through AutoGen to a third-party model provider
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not enforced in the model provider
mitigations: Block regulated data from AutoGen prompts
Use a DPA-approved model provider
Minimize logged prompt content
Document retention settings for both systems
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention enforcement
